title: Synthetic Consumer Insight Generation with Large Language Models
subcategory: marketing / synthetic data validation with STM
task: Comparing LLM-generated and human projective-technique responses (tourism city perceptions)
problem: Whether LLM 'silicon samples' can replace costly human data for projective techniques that need associations and creative interpretation.
architecture: LLM responses generated for 5 cities x 3 projective tasks x 6 LLMs x 5 temperatures x 5 prompting strategies; compared with human responses using lexical, diversity and concentration metrics, regression models, and structural topic models (R stm, city as prevalence covariate; K chosen by held-out likelihood, exclusivity, semantic coherence and residuals).
llm_or_encoder: ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4.1, ChatGPT 5.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Grok 4.1, Mistral Medium 3.1

datasets.name: Human projective responses (five U.S. tourism cities)
datasets.details: r = 173 human responses per city and setting (student sample), cities Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Nashville, New Orleans and New York City

metrics: word count, vocabulary size, lexical diversity, Shannon entropy, hapax rate, Simpson concentration, Yule's K
STM held-out likelihood, exclusivity, semantic coherence, residuals
key_results: A 9-topic STM was selected for human word associations (highest held-out likelihood, local maxima of exclusivity and coherence).
LLM topics (Gemini 2.5, extended prompt with probabilities, T = 1.8) show high concordance with human topics but emphasise different themes (e.g. Nashville hot chicken).
LLM lexical diversity comes largely from compound adjectives rather than more diverse topics.
strengths: Uses topic models as a validation tool for synthetic text, not only as a discovery tool.
Large factorial design over models, prompts and temperatures.

limitations.text: Only short-answer projective tasks (word association, sentence completion); human sample from one university; no personas or demographic targeting.
Topic comparison between human and LLM responses is qualitative (no topic-alignment score) and limited to the word-association task.
